definitions.explanation: A court ruling where a prison sentence is imposed but its execution is delayed for a specified period. If the offender commits no further crimes during that period, the sentence is waived.

examples.japanese: ⟦{懲役|ちょうえき}→懲役：11087_choueki⟧⟦{二年|にねん}→二年：28862_ninen⟧、{執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ}⟦{三年|さんねん}→三年：10984_sannen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{判決|はんけつ}→判決：05906_hanketsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: A sentence of two years in prison with a three-year suspended sentence was handed down.

examples.japanese: {執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ}⟦{付|つ}き→付き：26333_tsuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{判決|はんけつ}→判決：05906_hanketsu⟧だった。
examples.english: It was a verdict with a suspended sentence.

examples.japanese: {執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ}⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{再|ふたた}び→再び：03600_futatabi⟧⟦{罪|つみ}→罪：03532_tsumi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{犯|おか}す→犯す：10059_okasu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{実刑|じっけい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: If you commit another crime during probation, you will serve the actual sentence.

notes:
{執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ} combines ⟦{執行|しっこう}→執行：18996_shikkou⟧ (execution/enforcement) and ⟦{猶予|ゆうよ}→猶予：13496_yuuyo⟧ (postponement/grace period).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ}⟦{付|つ}き→付き：26333_tsuki⟧ — with a suspended sentence
- {執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ}⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧ — during probation
- {執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく — to receive a suspended sentence
- {執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ}{期間|きかん} — probation period

In Japanese law, a {執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ} of 1 to 5 years can be granted for prison sentences of 3 years or less. The phrase ⟦{懲役|ちょうえき}→懲役：11087_choueki⟧X⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧、{執行猶予|しっこうゆうよ}Y⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧ is the standard format seen in news reports about criminal verdicts.
